name: Fusion64 Product Quote Requests for WooCommerce
author: Fusion64

sections.description:
Some products don’t have a fixed price: bulk orders, wholesale buyers, custom sizes, trade customers. Fusion64 Product Quote Requests lets shoppers collect several products in a quote list and send it to you with their details.

Each request is saved as a normal WooCommerce order with the status Quote requested, so there is nothing new to learn. Open it, change the prices, add shipping if needed, and choose Send quote to customer. The customer gets the standard WooCommerce invoice email with a link to pay online.

Features

  • “Request a quote” button on product pages, for all products, chosen categories, or single products
  • Two modes: quote button next to Add to cart, or quote only (hides the price and Add to cart button)
  • Quote list with several products, quantities and variations
  • Simple form: name and email, plus phone, company and message (each optional, required or hidden)
  • Email to the shop for every request, with an optional copy to the shopper
  • Quotes are WooCommerce orders: edit prices, then send a payment link in one click
  • Quote requests are kept out of WooCommerce Analytics revenue until they are paid
  • Spam protection without a CAPTCHA (hidden honeypot field and an hourly limit per visitor)
  • Works with classic and block themes, and with High-Performance Order Storage (HPOS)

How it works

  1. A shopper clicks “Request a quote” on a product. It goes into their quote list.
  2. On the Request a Quote page they adjust quantities, fill in the form and send it.
  3. You get an email. The request appears under WooCommerce > Orders as “Quote requested”.
  4. Edit the prices, click Recalculate, then pick “Send quote to customer” in Order actions.
  5. The customer pays through your normal checkout. The order continues like any other.

For developers

Filters: f64raq_enabled_for_product, f64raq_quote_only, f64raq_supported_types, f64raq_form_fields, f64raq_validate, f64raq_hourly_limit.
Actions: f64raq_before_quote_saved, f64raq_quote_created, f64raq_quote_sent, f64raq_form_before_submit, f64raq_settings_after, f64raq_save_settings.
sections.installation:
1. Install the plugin from the Plugins screen, or upload the folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate it. WooCommerce must be active. A “Request a Quote” page is created for you.
  3. Go to WooCommerce > Settings > Quotes to choose which products show the button.
sections.faq:
Where do I see quote requests?

Under WooCommerce > Orders. Filter by the status “Quote requested”. You also get an email for each one.

How do I send the customer a price?

Open the quote, change the line item prices (and add shipping or fees if you like), click Recalculate, then choose “Send quote to customer (with payment link)” under Order actions and click Update. The order moves to Pending payment and the customer receives the WooCommerce invoice email with a “Pay for this order” link.

Can customers buy directly as well?

Yes. In the default mode the quote button sits next to Add to cart. Choose “Quote only” if you want to hide the price and Add to cart button.

Does it reduce stock when a quote is requested?

No. Stock is only reduced when the customer pays, as with any WooCommerce order.

The quote page is missing.

Create a page with the shortcode [f64raq_quote] and select it under WooCommerce > Settings > Quotes.
